title: "pollinators.qmd"

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
set.seed(42)

#Read CSV files
insect_counts <- read_csv("data/insect_counts.csv")
flower_counts <- read_csv("data/flower_counts.csv")
site_metadata <- read_csv("data/site_metadata.csv")

#Number of unique sites
site_count <- nrow(site_metadata)
print(site_count)

#Count observations of insects
total_insects_observed <- insect_counts |> pull(n_observed) |> sum()
print(total_insects_observed)

#Observations for each insect species
insect_totals <- insect_counts |> group_by(species) |> summarise(n_obs = sum(n_observed))
insect_totals <- insect_totals |> arrange(desc(n_obs))
gt(head(insect_totals)) #Including 'head()' only takes the top 6 rows

#Filter 'insect_counts' data frame to include only the counts for H. tumulorum
ht_counts <- insect_counts |> filter(species == "Halictus tumulorum")
gt(head(ht_counts))

#Add column to show whether H. tumulorum detected at each site, then add to 'site_metadata' dataframe and write to 'ht_df' csv file
ht_df <- ht_counts |> mutate(detected = n_observed > 0)
ht_df <- ht_df |> inner_join(site_metadata)
gt(head(ht_df))
write_csv(ht_df, "output/ht_df.csv")

#Select relevant columns to explore temperature relationship
ht_temp_df <- ht_df |>
  select(x1km_square, detected, min_temp_coldest_month)
gt(head(ht_temp_df))

#Calculate mean and standard deviation for number of observations for sites with and without H. tumulorum
ht_temp_summ <- ht_temp_df |>
  group_by(detected) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(min_temp_coldest_month),
    sd = sd(min_temp_coldest_month),
    count = n()
  )

# Separate present and absent sites
present <- ht_temp_summ |>
  filter(detected == TRUE)

absent <- ht_temp_summ |>
  filter(detected == FALSE)

gt(ht_temp_summ)
gt(present)
gt(absent)

#Draw a box plot to show this data
ggplot(ht_df, aes(x = min_temp_coldest_month, y = detected, fill = detected)) + geom_boxplot() + ggtitle("Minimum Temperature with and without H. tumulorum") + xlab("Minimum temperature (°C)") + ylab("Presence of H. tumulorum") + theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
#Running a t-test
ttest_ht_temp <- t.test(min_temp_coldest_month ~ detected, data = ht_temp_df, var.equal = TRUE)
print(ttest_ht_temp)

#Simulating the t-distribution
#First, simulate 1000 observations with 74 degrees of freedom
df74 <- rt(1000, df = 74)

#Create a data frame where this set of observations forms a column
t_dist <- tibble(simulated = df74)

#Plot results
ggplot(
  t_dist,
  aes(x = simulated)
) +
  geom_density() +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(
      ttest_ht_temp$statistic,
      -ttest_ht_temp$statistic
    ),
    color = "red"
  ) +
  ggtitle("Density of t-distribution - Simulated and Observed") +
  xlab("t") +
  ylab("Density") +
  theme_minimal()

#Calculate an approximated p-value - proportion of observations which are at least 5.726 from 0 in either direction
p_lower_sim <- sum(t_dist$simulated <= ttest_ht_temp$statistic) #ttest_ht_temp$statistic extracts the test statistic from the t-test 
p_upper_sim <- sum(t_dist$simulated >= -ttest_ht_temp$statistic)

p_sim <- (p_lower_sim + p_upper_sim) / nrow(t_dist)

print(p_sim) #p-value is 0 with 1000 observations

#Calculate the probability of getting a value which is not 0 given p-value = 2.07e-07
prob_no_extreme <- (1 - ttest_ht_temp$p.value)^1000
prob_at_least_one <- 1 - prob_no_extreme

print(prob_at_least_one)

#Calculate exact p-value using t-distribution cumulative probability function pt()
p_lower <- pt(ttest_ht_temp$statistic, 74)
p_upper <- 1 - pt(-ttest_ht_temp$statistic, 74)

pval <- p_lower + p_upper

print(pval) #This is the exact p-value calculated in out t-test

#Simulating confidence intervals
# Find the real difference for comparison
true_diff <- pull(present, mean) - pull(absent, mean)

# Vector to store the results
res_vec <- c()

for (i in seq_len(1000)) {
  # Simulate the two samples
  sample_present <- rnorm(pull(present, count), mean = pull(present, mean), sd = pull(present, sd))
  sample_absent <- rnorm(pull(absent, count), mean = pull(absent, mean), sd = pull(absent, sd))

  # Put the results into a data frame
  df <- tibble(
    sample = c(
      rep("sample_1", length(sample_present)),
      rep("sample_2", length(sample_absent))
    ),
    min_temp_coldest_month = c(sample_present, sample_absent)
  )

  # Run the t-test
  ttest_res <- t.test(min_temp_coldest_month ~ sample,
    data = df,
    var.equal = TRUE
  )

  # Extract the confidence interval
  ci_lower <- ttest_res$conf.int[1]
  ci_upper <- ttest_res$conf.int[2]

  # Check if the result is in the confidence interval or not
  res_in_ci <- between(true_diff, ci_lower, ci_upper)

  # Store the result
  res_vec <- c(res_vec, res_in_ci)
}

#Percentage of confidence intervals that contain the true difference
perc <- (sum(res_vec)/length(res_vec))*100
print(perc)
#In this simulation, the 95% confidence interval contained the true difference between the population means 94% of the time. This is close to the expected 95%, illustrating that when we repeatedly sample from a population and calculate a 95% confidence interval, approximately 95% of those intervals contain the true population value.

#Calculating confidence intervals using simulated t-distribution
#Plot simulated t-distribution
ggplot(
  t_dist,
  aes(x = simulated)
) +
  geom_density() +
  ggtitle("Density of t-distribution - Simulated") +
  xlab("t") +
  ylab("Density")

#Find middle 95%
quantile_df <- t_dist |>
  summarise(
    lower = quantile(simulated, 0.025),
    upper = quantile(simulated, 0.975)
  )
gt(quantile_df)

#Add to density plot
ggplot(
  t_dist,
  aes(x = simulated)
) +
  geom_density() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(pull(quantile_df, lower), pull(quantile_df, upper)), color = "blue") +
  ggtitle("Density of t-distribution -\nSimulated with simulated quantiles") +
  xlab("t") +
  ylab("Density") +
  theme_minimal()

#Calculate exact values using the cumulative distribution function qt()
lower_exact <- qt(0.025, 74)
upper_exact <- qt(0.975, 74)
print(lower_exact)
print(upper_exact)

#Plot exact values to show that their absolute values are identical as the t-distribution is symmetric
ggplot(
  t_dist,
  aes(x = simulated)
) +
  geom_density() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(lower_exact, upper_exact), color = "orange") +
  ggtitle("Density of t-distribution -\nSimulated with theoretical quantiles") +
  xlab("t") +
  ylab("Density") +
  theme_minimal()
#This absolute value is the critical t value or t-star

#Multiply t-star by the standard error of the t-test to convert t-star into the units of the response variable
tstar <- upper_exact
SE <- ttest_ht_temp$stderr
confint_rv_units <- tstar * SE
print(confint_rv_units)
#This tells us how far we need to go above and below our estimated difference between means to obtain 95% confidence interval
diff_means <- pull(absent, mean) - pull(present, mean)
lower_cint <- diff_means - confint_rv_units
upper_cint <- diff_means + confint_rv_units
print(c(lower_cint, upper_cint))
#This gives us our lower value of -1.7011 and upper value of -0.8228 as above.
```
```{r}
#Create the linear model for the data
lm_ht <- lm(min_temp_coldest_month ~ detected, data = ht_temp_df)

#Summarise the linear model
summ_lm_ht <- summary(lm_ht)
print(summ_lm_ht)

#Print confidence interval for the slope of the line in the linear model
ci <- confint(lm_ht)
print(ci)
#This is identical to out t-test values above
#Conclusion: There is evidence that minimum temperature differs according to the presence or absence of H. tumulorum (𝛽 = 1.26°C, 95% CI [0.82, 1.7]°C, 𝑡(74) = 5.73, 𝑝 = 2.07e-07, 𝑅2 = 0.307). Sites where H. tumulorum is present have a mean minimum temperature approximately 1.26°C higher than sites where it is absent. The model explains approximately 30.7% of the variation in minimum temperature.

#Visualising our linear model
ht_temp_df <- ht_temp_df |>
  mutate(detected_num = as.numeric(detected))

overall_mean <- ht_temp_df |>
  pull(min_temp_coldest_month) |>
  mean()

ggplot(ht_temp_df, aes(
  x = detected_num,
  y = min_temp_coldest_month
)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = overall_mean), color = "red") +
  ggtitle("Minimum temperature vs H. tumulorum detection - Observed and Fitted") +
  xlab("H. tumulorum detected") +
  ylab("Minimum temperature (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()

#Run an ANOVA on this linear model
anova_lm <- anova(lm_ht)
print(anova_lm)
#Same linear model so by definition same confidence interval and hence identical p-value

#Proportion of variance explained by the model relative to the variance of the response variable using sums of squares in the ANOVA output
SS_model <- anova_lm["detected", "Sum Sq"]
SS_res <- anova_lm["Residuals", "Sum Sq"]
prop_var <- SS_model / (SS_res + SS_model)
print(prop_var) # This is the same as R^2 in the linear model above
#Conclusion: There is evidence that minimum temperature in the coldest month differs between sites where H. tumulorum is present and sites where it is absent (𝐹(1, 74) = 32.79, 𝑝 = 2.07e-07, 𝑅2 = 0.307). The model explains approximately 30.7% of the variation in minimum temperature in the coldest month.
```
```{r}
#Plot a box plot to show mean insect mass at sites dominated by different insect families
ggplot(site_metadata, aes(x= dominant_family, y = mean_insect_mass, fill = dominant_family)) + geom_boxplot() + ggtitle("Mean insect mass at sites dominated by different insect families - Observed") + xlab("Insect Family") + ylab("Mean insect mass (g)") + theme_minimal()

#Create a linear model for the association between mean insect mass and dominant family
lm_mass_domfam <- lm(mean_insect_mass ~ dominant_family, data = site_metadata)
summary(lm_mass_domfam)

#Run an ANOVA on this linear model
anova_mass_domfam <- anova(lm_mass_domfam)
print(anova_mass_domfam)
#Conclusion: There is evidence that mean insect mass differs among dominant insect families (𝐹(3, 72) = 14.72, 𝑝 = 0.00000014), 𝑅2 = 0.38). Dominant insect family explains approximately 38% of the variation in mean insect mass among sites.

#Simulating an F distribution
#First, sample 1000 observations with 3 numerator degrres of freedom and 72 denominator degrees of freedom and store as a column in a dataframe
df_3_72 <- rf(n = 1000, df1 = 3, df2 = 72)
f_dist <- tibble(simulated = df_3_72)

#Plot the F-distribution
fstat <- anova_mass_domfam["dominant_family", "F value"]
ggplot(f_dist, aes(x = simulated)) + geom_density() + geom_vline(xintercept = fstat, color = "red") + ggtitle("Density of F-distribution - Simulated and Observed") + xlab("F") + ylab("Density") + theme_minimal()

#Calculate an approximate p-value from simulated data - proportion of simulated F-values greater than or equal to F-statistic calculated from the data (14.72)
p_above_sim <- sum(f_dist$simulated >= fstat)
p_sim <- p_above_sim / nrow(f_dist)
print(p_sim) #As previously, value is 0 at such a low p-value and 1000 simulations

#Calculate the exact p-value using the F-distribution cumulative probability function pf()
p_below <- pf(fstat, 3, 72)
p_exact <- 1 - p_below
print(p_exact) #Exact p-value calculated by ANOVA
```
